outcome: The general n-dimensional Hadwiger covering conjecture (every convex body in R^n covered by at most 2^n smaller homothetic copies) remains open for n>=3, but several in-window results moved bounds or settled restricted classes: (1) explicit upper bounds on H_n for small dimensions improved (arXiv:2404.00547, April 2024, published in Canadian Mathematical Bulletin 2025); (2) the illumination/covering conjecture was confirmed for the specific class of 'cap bodies' in all dimensions (arXiv:2510.25968, Oct 2025); (3) a very fresh, undigested, single-author preprint (arXiv:2609.23913, Sept 20 2026) claims an asymptotically optimal exponential growth rate for the covering number as n->infinity, but this is not a resolution of the exact 2^n conjecture and has had essentially no time for expert review.
summary: The general Hadwiger covering conjecture (H_n = 2^n for n>=3, equality only for parallelepipeds) is still open, and remains so on the live Wikipedia article as of this research. Within the 26 Jan 2024 - present window I found three distinct pieces of movement, none of which involve AI. First, arXiv:2404.00547 (submitted April 2024, later published in the Canadian Mathematical Bulletin in 2025) improved explicit small-dimension upper bounds (H5<=933, H6<=6137, H7<=41377, H8<=284096, and symmetric-body variants), using John-ellipsoid covering arguments and quermassintegral estimates -- classic computer-algebra-free convex geometry, no AI. This is squarely `progress`: a bound moved, general conjecture untouched. Second, arXiv:2510.25968 (Arman, Kaire, Prymak; submitted 29 Oct 2025, revised Dec 2025 and Aug 2026) confirms Hadwiger's conjecture for the restricted class of 'cap bodies' (convex hulls of a ball and finitely many external points) in all dimensions, using probabilistic arguments and, for 4<=n<=15, SageMath-based computer-assisted linear programming -- no AI/ML anywhere in the method. Cap bodies are a proper subclass of all convex bodies, so per Section 3.1 this is a genuine restricting case (the conjecture is now known for that whole subclass in every dimension) rather than a variant with changed hypotheses; I classify it as a case within `partial`-type territory, but since the small-dimension bound result independently qualifies for `progress` and represents an unambiguous, undisputed bound movement on the *general* open conjecture, I use `progress` as the overall status to avoid overstating the cap-bodies result as broader resolution than it is (see competing_reading). Third, and most striking: arXiv:2609.23913, submitted by a single author (Yegor Gorodzha) only two days before this research was conducted (20 Sept 2026), claims to establish 'the optimal exponential rate' for the covering number as n->infinity via a fractional-illumination / overlap-energy argument. This is emphatically not a resolution of the exact conjecture (it is an asymptotic growth-rate statement, leaving the precise multiplicative structure and all specific dimensions open), it has had no time for any expert digestion, and I could find no academic footprint for the author beyond a Kaggle profile and a YouTube channel -- red flags that argue for extreme caution rather than for treating it as a credited advance. I have not counted it toward the status decision; I flag it in case a future pass wants to track its fate. No source anywhere -- author accounts, acknowledgements, or secondary coverage -- mentions any AI or machine-learning system in connection with any of these three results; all computation described is either probabilistic-combinatorial by hand or classical LP/computer-algebra (SageMath), not AI in the sense used by this dataset.
competing_reading: One could argue the cap-bodies result (arXiv:2510.25968) alone should drive status to `partial` rather than `progress`, since it is a genuine, complete resolution for an entire (admittedly narrow) subclass of convex bodies in all dimensions, which is a stronger and more definite kind of movement than an incremental bound. I lean toward `progress` as the umbrella status because the problem as Wikipedia states it is about *all* n-dimensional convex bodies, and the aggregate picture across all in-window results is best described as movement on bounds/sub-cases rather than any resolved fragment that a careful reader would say meaningfully narrows the general question people actually care about (arbitrary convex bodies in fixed low dimensions, where the conjecture is completely open). A downstream pass could reasonably override this to `partial`, crediting Arman-Kaire-Prymak, with resolution_direction `confirmed` for the cap-body case.
what_would_settle_it: Whether an expert survey or the Wikipedia article itself, once updated, describes the cap-bodies theorem as 'resolving a case of Hadwiger's conjecture' versus discussing it as a separate strand of the illumination-conjecture literature would settle the partial-vs-progress line. Independently, watching whether arXiv:2609.23913 attracts any citation, review, or refutation in the coming months would settle whether it belongs in the record at all.

judgement.doubts: The record's event, credited_humans and direction already describe the cap-bodies result; only the status was held back to 'progress' by a judgement that the case is narrow, which §4 does not allow — a settled case is partial whatever its size. The Gorodzha preprint is a bound at most and cannot outrank partial; its fate is unknown. The record could not rule out an AI disclosure in its body.
